evidence.field: 甲金文字形；《說文》；形義通解；早期用例
evidence.text: The entry interprets 系’s oracle-bone and bronze forms as a hand (爪/又) holding connected silk, with a binding/connection sense. It records alternatives: a proposal that 系 is an early form of 攣, and the received 說文 analysis 从糸、丿聲. CUHK argues instead that seal-script 丿 is a reduced 爪 and calls the phonetic analysis doubtful. It cites oracle-bone ritual-name and place/state-name uses and a bronze personal-name use, but does not date those inscriptions individually.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「系」

evidence.text: The entry gives 系’s received 《說文》 analysis as 从糸、丿聲, and identifies 係 with modern Mandarin xì and Guangyun 胡計. Its account interprets the 係 oracle-bone graph as 人 plus 糸, sometimes with hands, for binding a person; it describes 係 as a verb in oracle-bone inscriptions and notes a later bronze arrangement of 人 and 糸 that it considers the basis of the seal form. This source evidence supports a phonetic role for 系 within 係 separately from disputed claims about 系’s own origin.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「係」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry reports 《說文》’s 係 analysis “絜束也。从人从系，系亦聲” and provides a variant discussion, including a claim that some written forms arose through scribal confusion of 人 and 彳 or through a 糸 variant. This is evidence for the received phonetic account, not a resolution of 系’s paleographic origin.
evidence.title: [A00165] 係 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 《說文》；《禮記》《荀子》《周禮》《西京賦》 examples
evidence.text: The entry gives 繫’s received formation as 糸 plus phonetic 毄 and glosses its early sense as tying/fastening. It lists textual examples for confinement, hanging, concern, connection, and relation/dependence. These cited texts illustrate senses but do not by themselves establish a dated sequence of semantic change or a historical graphic simplification into 系.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「繫」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry identifies 繫 as 糸 with phonetic 毄 and gives readings xì and jì with senses including connect, hang, concern, imprison, and tie. It lists 系 as a variant/counterpart. The page supports a modern orthographic relationship in its variant list but does not establish a historical chronology for that relationship.
evidence.title: [A03181] 繫 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The inspected file description identifies ACC-s05880.svg as a modern vector drawing depicting 係 in Shuowen seal-script style. It cites the ancient-character data source and marks the SVG representation public domain; the page supplies the exact original file link: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/38/ACC-s05880.svg. This is a seal-style redraw, not a photograph of an ancient artifact.

The exact original file URL is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ac/%E7%B3%BB-seal.svg. This is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

evidence.text: Direct opens of official Unihan records for 系 (U+7CFB), 係 (U+4FC2), and 繫 (U+7E6B) were attempted but failed in this session. The supplied local rows give xì for each, but are local metadata rather than externally verified Unicode evidence. Modern reading similarity alone does not establish an ancient phonetic relationship.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup

evidence.text: The authors’ documentation distinguishes medieval-dictionary MC transcription from reconstructed OC. Exact local rows provided in the packet are 系 MC hejH, OC *[m]-kˤek-s; 係 MC kejH, OC *kˤek-s; and 繫 MC kejH / OC *Cə.kˤe-s plus MC hejH / OC *m-kˤek-s. These rows were locally supplied, not exposed in the inspected PDF. The system’s documentation does not establish the phonetic relationship itself.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

search_audit.query: 系 甲骨文 金文 說文 从糸丿聲 字形 CUHK 字源; 係 甲骨文 金文 說文 絜束 从人从系 系亦聲 字形; 繫 說文 从糸毄聲 甲骨文 金文 字源; site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File 系-seal.svg 係-seal.svg ACC-s05880.svg
search_audit.outcome: Opened the CUHK 系, 係 and 繫 entries and the two MOE entries. Commons search results exposed exact descriptions for the 係 and 系 seal redraws; source pages were verified via their descriptions. Key conclusions: 系’s early hand-and-threads explanation is disputed against 說文; 系’s phonetic role in 係 is explicitly documented.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File 系 seal.svg character 系 seal script
search_audit.outcome: Search result gave the file description, depicted character, style, source notes and license text.

Search result gave the exact description page and original image URL. Separate open calls to the Commons pages and direct upload.wikimedia.org assets returned cache/access errors; the exact description-page result itself contained the metadata and original link.

gaps: 系’s earliest inscriptional forms and their dates were not independently dated in the inspected character entry. Its proposed hand-plus-connected-threads interpretation is a source assertion, while the alternative 攣-origin proposal and the received 說文 丿-as-phonetic account remain in tension; no adjudication is established here.

The reported oracle-bone ritual, place/state, and bronze personal-name uses are not dated milestones for the lexical senses ‘thread’, ‘connection’, ‘lineage’, or ‘system’. CUHK cites a Han Shu lineage example, but intermediate semantic chronology and a historical sequence for ‘system’ remain unestablished.

係 has an early bind/tie interpretation and a source-attested 系 phonetic role. Its later connection and copular uses are cited in textual sources, but their earliest attestation dates and semantic transitions are not established by this research.

繫’s tie, confine, hang, concern, connect, and relation senses are cited from received texts; the inspected entries do not provide dated manuscript attestations that establish their order or demonstrate that 系 is a regular graphic simplification of 繫.

Local Baxter–Sagart readings retain distinct initial/vocalic details for 系 and 係 (and multiple rows for 繫); exact online rows were not opened. Do not merge the local dataset’s notation with other reconstructions or infer a sound change beyond what sources support.
Official Unicode Unihan pages for the three characters could not be accessed, so their local kMandarin xì rows are not externally click-through verified in this report.

The Commons file-description search results were readable, but subsequent direct opens of the Commons pages and upload image URLs failed with cache/access errors. The file records remain source-page leads; no image pixels were inspected.
